acceptance: docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md and the todo skill's batch reference state that each batch leader runs as its own top-level session (or with its own TODO_DB_ACTOR), and that members never run as subagents of a leader's session.
The same docs say to measure the combined member diff with batch-status/brief sizes before register_batch, not to estimate it.
Batch tooling refuses, or the leader procedure detects, a member landing whose tracker writes came from the batch owner's principal; the check is exercised by a test.
The four batches registered on 2026-11-04 are checked for member-originated tracker writes before their final PRs are armed, and the result is recorded here.
context: 2026-11-05 audit of the four active batches (arrow-dataframe-roundtrips, native-bulk-load-remainder, native-bulk-load-sql, tpch-refresh-path), read from each member item's tracker session history since its batch's integration_log start. Every write carries the one shared owner principal (...8b868951fc54003923be2571), so attribution is inferred from timing and content. Each member shows: the leader's metadata update within seconds of registration, then take and prepare a few seconds apart at landing. There are no writes in the window between member creation and landing. tpch-refresh-path also has one post-prepare update on each of its four members within 14 seconds (14:43:46-14:44:00Z). Those are verification-summary context notes, consistent with a leader sweep. Conclusion: no evidence of member-originated tracker writes; the shared identity means this cannot be proven.
description: todo-db derives each worker's principal from a per-process session id (todo_db/mcp/identity.py), and omp subagents borrow their parent's MCP connection. Four parallel batch leaders that ran as subagents of one session therefore registered the same owner and serialized on its single live-claim slot. If members also ran as subagents of a leader's session, the E_BATCH_OWNER refusal could not separate them from the owner, because the tracker sees one identity. The todo skill already says a member must not share the leader's server or actor, but nothing states how sessions must be launched to achieve that, and nothing detects a breach.
